## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #13422: Hook spawn cwd validation — CRITICAL security/stability fix (CRITICAL HIGH ~6h from 2026-08-30)

- **What**: Cline prevented hook spawn failures from crashing the entire cline-core process. Hook child-process spawn failure emitted "error" on HookProcess with no listener registered, which Node's EventEmitter turns into uncaught exception — killing the entire core process instead of failing the one hook. Guard: check listenerCount before emit so rejection (which StdioHookRunner handles) is the only propagation path. Trigger was workspace root that no longer exists passed as spawn cwd: Node reports nonexistent cwd as misleading ENOENT on launcher binary ("spawn /bin/sh ENOENT"). Validate cwd existence before spawning, fall back to no explicit cwd with warning. Updated: fail hooks with missing cwd instead of relocating. Running hook with missing cwd from host process's own cwd would let relative paths read/write unrelated location (e.g. IDE install directory). Reject before spawning with error naming missing directory; runner reports hook as failed, task continues. Carry pre-spawn failure messages into HookExecutionError details so cause is not reduced to bare "exited with code 1".
- **Why**: Hook spawn failure should fail the hook, not crash the orchestrator. Nonexistent cwd should reject with descriptive error, not relocate to process.cwd() and let hook read/write wrong location. Security fix.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13422 (fix(vscode): prevent hook spawn failures from crashing the core process)
- **Category**: tool (hooks / spawn)
- **Size**: CRITICAL HIGH (~6h — Alexi has NO hooks implementation yet. src/hooks/ does not exist, src/core/ has no hooks/. Pattern is CRITICAL for when hooks are added: (1) validate cwd exists before spawn (fs.existsSync on cwd path, reject with descriptive error if missing), (2) guard "error" event emit behind listenerCount check (check emitter.listenerCount('error') > 0 before emit('error', err)), (3) fail with descriptive error instead of relocating to process.cwd() (no fallback cwd, descriptive rejection names missing directory), (4) carry pre-spawn failure details into hook execution error (wrap spawn error with context: hook name, missing cwd path, original error message). Security fix — hook running from wrong cwd is dangerous. Defer until hooks implementation prioritized, but remember pattern).

#### 2. Cline #13680: Langfuse tracer detection minify survivability — CRITICAL defensive pattern (CRITICAL MODERATE ~4h from 2026-08-30)

- **What**: Cline fixed Langfuse telemetry initialization to survive minified release builds. Release binaries compiled with minify enabled rename classes, so initializeLangfuseTelemetry's constructor-name guard never matched "ProxyTracerProvider" and silently returned readiness=false in production (dev unminified source worked). Replace constructor-name comparisons with checks that survive minification: detect proxy structurally via getDelegate, distinguish recording provider from no-op fallback by lifecycle methods, confirm NodeTracerProvider registration by object identity. When foreign provider owns global slot, attach Langfuse span processor if it accepts processors, else shut down orphaned provider and report rejection. Verified by bundling module with Bun minify:true against real OpenTelemetry packages: previous code reproduces readiness=false (provider class name mangles to "H2"), new code initializes with readiness=true.
- **Why**: Telemetry initialization should survive minified production builds. Constructor-name checks break when minifier renames classes.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13680 (fix(llms): make Langfuse tracer detection survive minified release builds)
- **Category**: tool (telemetry / minify)
- **Size**: CRITICAL MODERATE (~4h — Alexi has NO Langfuse integration currently (no Langfuse imports in src/). Pattern is CRITICAL for ANY telemetry integration using constructor-name checks. Minification renames classes, so `instanceof ClassName` works but `obj.constructor.name === 'ClassName'` fails. If Alexi adds Langfuse (or OpenTelemetry, Sentry, Datadog, any telemetry with class-based initialization), use structural checks instead: (1) detect proxy via getDelegate method existence (`typeof provider.getDelegate === 'function'`), (2) distinguish recording provider from no-op by lifecycle methods (`typeof provider.shutdown === 'function'`), (3) confirm registration by object identity (`trace.getTracerProvider() === myProvider`), (4) when foreign provider owns global slot, attach processor if it accepts them (`typeof provider.addSpanProcessor === 'function'`). Defensive pattern for minified builds. Defer until Langfuse integration is prioritized, but remember pattern for any telemetry integration).

#### 3. Cline #13639: Remote MCP connect timeout — prevent session create stalls (HIGH ~4h)

- **What**: Remote (SSE/streamable HTTP) MCP connects run on the session.create critical path, which the hub caps at 30s. Without a connect budget an unreachable server spent the full 60s default request timeout (with the SSE transport stuck in a reconnect loop), stalling session.create past the hub deadline and tearing the whole session down — interactive TUI exited and one-shot runs failed. Stdio servers already have a bounded initialize budget for exactly this reason; give URL clients the same treatment with a 10s default connect budget that an explicit timeout overrides in either direction. Fixes #13597.
- **Why**: Remote MCP servers should not stall session creation for 60s on connection failure. Bound connect budget to prevent TUI exit / one-shot run failures.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13639 (Fix CLI crash when a remote MCP server is offline but enabled)
- **Category**: mcp (connect timeout)
- **Size**: HIGH (~4h — Alexi has MCP support (src/mcp/). Verify if remote MCP has connect timeout. If not, add bounded connect budget (10s default, overridable via explicit timeout config in mcp-servers.json) for SSE/streamable HTTP transports. Check src/mcp/ for remote MCP client initialization, ensure URL-based MCP connects do not block session.create indefinitely when server is unreachable. Stdio servers already have bounded initialize budget, extend same pattern to remote transports).

#### 4. Cline #13420: Session history FTS — indexed full-text search (HIGH ~10h from 2026-08-28)

- **What**: Cline added indexed full-text search for session history via command bar (Cmd/Ctrl+P) instead of a sidebar-local cmdk dialog that eagerly loaded the entire session history via loadAllSessions(). CommandDialog gains a shouldFilter passthrough so server-ranked FTS hits are displayed as-is. Includes hardening: evict failed restoration sessions from search, preserve deletion when search eviction fails, address review feedback, preserve search suppression during reconciliation. Tests cover sidecar search fallback on hub timeout and rejection.
- **Why**: Session history search should not eagerly load entire session history. Indexed FTS provides fast search with server-ranked results.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13420 (feat: add searchable session history)
- **Category**: command (session search)
- **Size**: HIGH (~10h — Alexi has session management (src/core/sessionManager.ts, src/cli/commands/sessions.ts). CLI tool uses terminal UI, not VS Code sidebar. Indexed FTS may be overkill for CLI (terminal users typically have fewer sessions than VS Code users with persistent sidebar). Evaluate need: if Alexi session list grows large (100+ sessions), indexed search improves performance. If session count stays low (< 50), simple grep over session files is sufficient. Check src/cli/commands/sessions.ts for current session search implementation. If eager loading entire session list is a bottleneck, implement lazy loading + incremental search before full FTS index. Defer until session list performance becomes a problem).

#### 5. Cline #13614: Global rules path discovery — WSL/headless compatibility (MODERATE ~3h)

- **What**: Cline fixed global rules path discovery for WSL/headless installs. VS Code Rules tab resolves Documents folder via 'xdg-user-dir DOCUMENTS', which prints bare $HOME when no user-dirs config exists (WSL/headless installs), so it reads and writes global rules at ~/Cline/Rules. The SDK's rule search paths only covered ~/Documents/Cline/Rules, so those rules never reached the system prompt. Add the missing path to the search list. Fixes #13542.
- **Why**: Global rules should be discovered at ~/Cline/Rules in addition to ~/Documents/Cline/Rules for WSL/headless compatibility.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13614 (fix(shared): discover global rules at ~/Cline/Rules)
- **Category**: config (rules path discovery)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~3h — Alexi may have similar issue if global rules path discovery is hard-coded. Check where Alexi reads global rules (likely src/config/ or src/core/). If Alexi only checks ~/Documents/Alexi/Rules (or equivalent), add ~/Alexi/Rules as fallback for WSL/headless installs where xdg-user-dir DOCUMENTS returns bare $HOME. Pattern: try ~/Documents/<tool>/Rules first, fall back to ~/<tool>/Rules if no user-dirs config exists. Linux/WSL compatibility fix).
